own_original_text:
Whereas, the Secretary of Agriculture having submitted for my approval a Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry and having rendered his report and recommendations and findings thereon;

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 10, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby find that:

1. Due notice and opportunity for hearings to interested parties have been given pursuant to the provisions of the act and regulations thereunder, upon a code of fair competition presented by the Secretary of Agriculture upon his own motion pursuant to section 3 (d) of the act, and Executive orders under the act; and,

2. Hearings have been held upon said code, pursuant to such notice and pursuant to the pertinent provisions of the act and regulations thereunder; and,

3. Said code of fair competition constitutes a code of fair competition, as contemplated by the act and complies in all respects with the pertinent provisions of the act, including clause (2) of subsection (a) of section 3 of title I of the act; and,

4. It appears, after due consideration, that said code of fair competition will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress as declared in section 1 of title I of the act,

Now, Therefore, I, Franklin D. Roosevelt, President of the United States, pursuant to the authority vested in me by title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act, approved June 16, 1933, and otherwise, do hereby approve said Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

December 9, 1933.

versions.research_rationale:
Executive Order 6487-B (December 9, 1933) is a approval of the Code of Fair Competition for the Distilled Spirits Rectifying Industry under section 3 of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act. Read in full from the held American Presidency Project transcription (page record checked; identity, date and subject confirmed against the census register and the WPA 1944 list); the order's own text states no limit on the approval. Its command depends entirely on the code approval, so its first end is the repeal of the code-approval and code-enforcement provisions of Title I by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 on June 14, 1935, applying SHARED_ANALYSIS.md and its adjudication; Schechter (May 27, 1935) is recorded as a validity characterization only.
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"The order states no period, \"until\" date, condition or provisional approval that limits the approval, and no stay or postponement to a fixed date. Held later orders naming the code are EO 6685 (April 20, 1934), EO 6812 (August 4, 1934), EO 6945 (January 10, 1935), EO 6954 (January 31, 1935), EO 7017 (April 19, 1935) and EO 7022 (April 20, 1935). I read the operative sentence of each: each approves amendments and modifies the previous approval to include an approval of the code in its entirety as amended. None cancels, suspends, supersedes or revokes the approval, so each is a later event. No held text cites this order by number. No held record shows this code cancelled, suspended, superseded or revoked before June 14, 1935, and none shows a modification under section 10(b) that reached this order's command. June 16, 1935 is not an end, because section 1 of S.J. Res. 113 replaced that expiry with April 1, 1936. Schechter (May 27, 1935) is a validity characterization, not an end date.","independent_command_check":"No appointment, delegation, direction to a government agency, report direction or other command independent of the code approval appears. The \"Approval recommended\" and signature lines command nothing.","savings_check":"Read S.J. Res. 113 section 2 and its proviso and NIRA section 5 in the packet excerpts. No held source continues this approval, a prosecution under it or any command of this order after June 14, 1935; accrued acts, liabilities and the section 5 exemption for completed action are recorded as transferred or accrued and not as continued operation.","scope_check":"The machine inventory has four clauses, items 1 to 4, which are the President's numbered findings (notice and hearing, hearings held, the code complies with section 3, the code will tend to effectuate the policy of Congress) and, at the end of item 4, the final approval. Findings command nothing. The only operative command is the final sentence approving the code, which is the single corrected clause (inventory correction recorded). The order also says the code was presented \"pursuant to section 3 (d) of the act\"; the order approves the code under Title I, so the section 3 analysis applies, and a prescription under section 3(d) was equally repealed by section 2 of S.J. Res. 113. The held transcription reads \"approved June 10, 1933\" in the first operative sentence and \"approved June 16, 1933\" in the final one; the act is dated June 16, 1933 and the discrepancy does not affect the command."}

savings_residuals.reason: Acts done and liabilities incurred under the approved code before June 14, 1935 are accrued consequences, and the section 5 exemption from the antitrust laws for action complying with an approved code taken while Title I was in effect is likewise an accrued effect for completed action. The proviso to section 2 of S.J. Res. 113 names agreements and action under them, not codes, and states no time limit; the held text does not settle whether it narrowed the section 5 exemption for past action under codes, and whatever exemption survives for past action is an accrued effect, not continued operation of this approval. Nothing in the held sources continues the approval after June 14, 1935.
